source_inspection_notes: Read controlled_delegatecall.py in full: only flags delegatecall()/callcode() whose DESTINATION address is 'tainted' (attacker-controllable). A delegatecall to a fixed, hardcoded, or owner-set-but-currently-static address -- which still violates EthTrust's unconditional 'MUST NOT contain the delegatecall() instruction' -- produces no finding. Same structural pattern as tx-origin/suicidal/encode-packed-collision in this batch: Slither's detector suite is built around 'dangerous usage', EthTrust's S-level text is built around 'mere presence'.

derivation_trace.analyzer_behavior: Flags delegatecall/callcode only when the destination is tainted by external input.
covered_cases: delegatecall to an attacker-influenceable address -- the classic proxy-hijack exploit shape
uncovered_cases: delegatecall to any fixed/hardcoded/admin-set-but-static address -- common in legitimate proxy patterns, still literally prohibited by EthTrust's S-level text (the proxy pattern is exactly what the Set-of-Overriding-Requirements, req-2-external-calls + req-2-documented, exists to legitimize)
derivation_trace.final_classification: PARTIAL_MATCH -- evidence collector for the taint-controlled subset only.
